CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules (workflow, r-package, ci, correctness, assurance) come from the r-skills plugin’s rules/, loaded at session start because of the marker above. Never copy them here. Where this file and a shared rule disagree, this file wins for this package. Cloud sessions do not load the plugin and run without them.

What this is

zulake opens a Delta Lake table where it is stored (Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 or Blob Storage, or local disk) and exposes everything the table’s log records as base data frames: versions, commits, live files with their partition values, statistics and deletion vectors, schema, protocol and properties, and the changes between versions. Reading data, with file pruning by partition and statistics, is the convenience on top. It is pure R over zujson, qio and zuhttp, with zuroar suggested for deletion vectors. It does not write, run queries, obtain Azure tokens or support stores other than Azure, and 0.1.0 does not read Iceberg.

The specification is .agents/design.md, adopted from RFC 0081. It outranks this file: CLAUDE.md orients, the design decides.

Current state

Scaffolded 2026-11-26 with create-pkg.sh. Stage 2 (log replay from commit 0, local disk only) is in: lake_open(), lake_is_table(), lake_load(), lake_version(). Stage 3 (inspection) adds the table, file and log functions of design §5, except lake_deletion_vectors(). Stage 4 (reading and pruning) adds lake_read(), lake_walk() and lake_count(footers = TRUE). Stage 5 adds deletion vectors (lake_deletion_vectors(), rows dropped on read, zuroar suggested) and name-mode column mapping on reads, and makes filters row-wise by construction. Stage 6 adds the Azure backend (R/azure.R, over zuhttp): the three URI forms, a bearer token from credentials(), and the request, emulator and live test layers. The roadmap in .agents/roadmap.md takes it to v0.1.0. 0.1.0 waits for zuhttp on CRAN and for zuroar 0.1.0 (design §9); local log replay, inspection and reading are built on local fixtures first.

Versions and dependents

v0.1.0 issue: created by pkg-roadmap. Sibling packages that will depend on this one: zugodb, through an extension that registers a delta format (design §3).

Commands

The shared commands, plus the suite as CI runs it (shuffled, seed printed, against the installed package):

R CMD INSTALL . && Rscript tools/ci-run-tests.R
ZULAKE_TEST_SEED=<seed> Rscript tools/ci-run-tests.R   # replay an order

Fixtures and oracle (uv 0.7.11; the order matters, PROVENANCE.md has it):

Rscript tools/fixtures/hostile.R                                   # hostile logs
(cd tools/oracle && uv run --frozen python ../fixtures/pack.py)    # repack the tar
(cd tools/oracle && uv run --frozen python answers.py)             # deltalake answers

Architecture

See .agents/design.md for the why. There is no native layer: no src/, by design (D1).

  • R/storage.R: the internal storage interface (list, get, get_range, head over paths relative to the table root) and its local backend; storage_for() picks one from the URI.
  • R/azure.R: the Azure backend (Blob REST through zuhttp), the URI forms (parse_azure_uri()), the credential registry that keeps the token out of the snapshot, the List Blobs parser, and the internal options zulake.azure_endpoint and zulake.azure_client (tests only).
  • R/log.R: what a _delta_log/ listing holds (log_entries()), JSON log files through zujson, _last_checkpoint.
  • R/replay.R: the replay plan (commits, log compaction files) and the reconciliation of actions into a state.
  • R/protocol.R: the reader-feature gate (D7) and partition-value checks.
  • R/timestamp.R: commit times and time travel by timestamp.
  • R/open.R: the exported functions and snapshot_build(), which documents the snapshot’s fields.
  • R/int64.R: integers past 2^53 - 1 kept as marked text through zujson (mark_numbers()), and turned into doubles, errors or integer64 (int64_values(), unmark_tree()).
  • R/values.R: the schema, partition values and statistics typed by Delta type.
  • R/filter.R: the filter plan (pruning subset, row-wise nodes, or a refusal), its outcomes per file from partition values and statistics, and the row filter.
  • R/compare.R: the exact comparator (decimal text), byte-order string comparison, and filter values turned into comparison keys.
  • R/dv.R: lake_deletion_vectors(), a vector’s bytes from its descriptor (Z85, UUID paths, ranges, CRC-32, magic) and its rows through zuroar, which is suggested: need_zuroar() refuses by name.
  • R/read.R: lake_read(), lake_walk(), the read pipeline (read_scan(), read_piece(), bind_pieces()), fetch_file() and the session cache.
  • R/table.R, R/files.R, R/log-inspect.R, R/print.R: the inspection functions and the print method.
  • R/conditions.R: zulake_abort() and the zulake_error_* classes.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • No compiled code (D1). The log is JSON and Parquet, which zujson and qio read; adding src/ changes the package’s CI and CRAN profile.
  • zulake never imports zugodb (D6). zugodb calls zulake; the reverse makes a dependency cycle.
  • The bearer token never leaves the request. It is not stored in a snapshot, printed, or included in an error or a recorded cassette (D4, acceptance criterion 4). A leak here is a credential leak.
  • Unknown or unsupported reader features are refused by name before any data is read (D7). Ignoring columnMapping in id mode or deletion vectors returns wrong rows silently.
  • A filter is row-wise by construction (D8). A call that is neither in the pruning subset nor in row_wise_functions is refused, never evaluated per file: per file it would give other rows than on the table.
  • zuroar is only suggested. Call it as zuroar:: after need_zuroar(); tests/zuroar-absent.R is the nosuggests check.
  • Statistics only decide what is downloaded. A file is pruned only on “cannot match”; the whole filter is then applied to rows, so a read is exact whatever the statistics say (design §6).
  • Names are for a table, not for Delta (D11). The lake_ functions, the snapshot class and the data frames they return must take Iceberg later without renaming.

Testing

tests/testthat.R runs every file with shuffle = TRUE after printing its seed, under R CMD check and covr alike; tools/ci-run-tests.R runs the same file from the source tree. The shuffle reorders every top-level expression of a test file, so shared functions go in helper-*.R, never at file scope. Fixtures (Stage 1, design §8): 31 Delta tables (14 copied from delta-rs, Apache-2.0; 2 changed from them; 15 zl-* written with deltalake 1.7.0) and 13 hostile logs, listed in tests/testthat/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md. They ship packed in tests/testthat/fixtures/delta-fixtures.tar, because Delta paths pass the 100 bytes a package tarball allows; the unpacked tables/ and hostile/ trees are in git only (.Rbuildignore), and are what you edit. deltalake 1.7.0’s answers for every table and version are in tests/testthat/fixtures/answers/ (fields and encoding in tools/oracle/README.md). Tests reach them through helper-oracle.R: fixture_table(name), local_fixture_copy(name), oracle_field(table, version, field), oracle_refusal() and expect_oracle(actual, table, version, field). Never edit an answer by hand, and never edit a tree without repacking (see Commands). inst/extdata/orders/, the example table the README, vignette and examples open, is pack.py’s copy of zl-orders (test-extdata.R); edit the fixture, never the copy.

Azure (helper-azure.R, tools/azurite/README.md): test-azure.R runs everywhere against azure_fake(), a zu_mock_transport() over the fixtures that records every request, and replays the cassettes in tests/testthat/fixtures/cassettes/, recorded from Azurite, never by hand. test-azure-emulator.R needs Azurite (ZULAKE_AZURITE_ENDPOINT) and skips without it; test-azure-live.R needs ZULAKE_AZURE_URI and ZULAKE_AZURE_TOKEN. No test may reach the network: a fake or a replaying cassette goes in zulake.azure_client.

Continuous integration

R-CMD-check.yaml calls r-actions r-cmd-check.yml@v1; coverage.yaml calls r-actions coverage.yml@v1 (badge on gh-pages); pkgdown.yaml builds and deploys the site. cran-release.yaml calls r-actions cran-release.yml@v1 when CRAN-SUBMISSION is pushed: it tags the submitted commit, creates the GitHub release and opens the .9000 bump. So CRAN-SUBMISSION is committed, not ignored. assurance.yaml calls r-actions assurance.yml@v1 with ungated-jobs: fail on .agents/assurance.md. The R-CMD-check caller adds Windows R-devel to the full profile’s runners and runs no container on a quick run (no src/; the full profile runs them). oracle.yaml is the package’s own workflow: it regenerates the deltalake answers, the hostile logs and the fixture tar, and fails on any diff. It runs on dispatch and on pull requests touching tools/oracle/, tools/fixtures/ or the fixtures (a paths filter, which assurance.yml counts as gated). azure-emulator.yaml (own, gated by changes.yml) starts Azurite over HTTPS with --oauth basic, uploads the fixtures, has deltalake read them (tools/oracle/azurite.py) and runs test-azure.R and test-azure-emulator.R with no skip allowed; it uploads the cassettes it records. azure-live.yaml (own, dispatch only, repository secrets) runs test-azure-live.R against ADLS Gen2 (#24).
